description:
Assess an edentulous site in the posterior mandible for implant feasibility based on inter-radicular space (root proximity).

Starting state: Blue Sky Plan is open with a mandibular CBCT scan loaded.

Task:
1. Identify a missing posterior tooth site (e.g., #19, #30, #18, or #31) where the adjacent teeth have visible roots.
2. Orient the view (Panoramic or Tangential) to clearly visualize the roots of the adjacent teeth in a single plane.
3. Measure the mesial-distal distance between the adjacent roots at the alveolar crest (Measurement A).
4. Measure the mesial-distal distance between the adjacent roots at 6mm apical to (below) the crest (Measurement B).
5. Determine if a 4.0mm implant is feasible. The required space is 7.0mm (4.0mm implant + 1.5mm safety buffer on each side). If BOTH measurements are >= 7.0mm, it is feasible.
6. Save a screenshot showing the view with both measurements visible to 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\root_space_analysis.png'.
7. Create a text report at 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\feasibility_report.txt' with the format:
   SITE_ANALYSIS
   Selected Site: [Tooth Number]
   Distance at Crest: [X.X] mm
   Distance at 6mm Depth: [Y.Y] mm
   4.0mm Implant Feasible: [YES/NO]
